key_insight: Multi4D uses a physics-informed neural network to convert complex 4D-STEM diffraction patterns at heterogeneous interfaces into accurate, orientation-agnostic crystallographic maps.
engineering_relevance: It can accelerate failure analysis and quality control in superconductors, alloys, and solid-state batteries by revealing nanoscale structural variation that drives performance and degradation.
method: Latent-space Diffusion Transformer performs physics-constrained style translation of multi-component diffraction data.
Rotation-invariant CNN classifies crystal orientation without being sensitive to sample rotation.
Derives an uncertainty-based entropy metric, Diffraction-Inferred Structural Complexity, to quantify local structural ambiguity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 98.82% classification accuracy and demonstrates high-fidelity mapping on complex interfaces down to single-nanometer spatial resolution.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and representativeness of training data, especially for highly disordered or unseen interface chemistries.
paper_title: Multi4D: an end-to-end neural network for structural determination at complex material interfaces
